args.root_cause: In `paginate()`, the slice end index is computed as `end = start + page_size - 1` and then used as an exclusive bound in `items[start:end]`. This drops the last item of every page. Each page is one item short, so the item at each index that is a multiple of page_size (minus one) is never returned on any page. With 11 items and page size 5, items 5, 10 (1-based: the 5th and 10th items) are skipped, matching the report's "same items go missing at a regular interval". The fix is `end = start + page_size` (or slice `items[start:start + page_size]`). The last partial page is unaffected in practice only because the off-by-one still drops one item there too (e.g. page 3 of 11 returns [11] correctly only because the slice stops at len, but full pages lose their final element).

evidence.quote:
start = (page_number - 1) * page_size
    end = start + page_size - 1
    return Page(
        items=items[start:end],

page = paginate(list(range(1, 12)), page_number=1, page_size=5)
    assert page.items == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
assert [1, 2, 3, 4] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]  Right contains one more item: 5
